name: VI Peel

image.caption: George VI postbox on Peel Lane, Egerton - geograph.org.uk - 7067592

lead: The VI Peel is a branded medium-depth chemical peel from the Vitality Institute, marketed for acne, pigment, sun damage, scars and fine lines. The payoff people want is clearer, more even, smoother skin.

The blend combines trichloroacetic acid, phenol, salicylic acid, tretinoin and vitamin C to exfoliate the epidermis and upper dermis, after which skin sheds and renews. Published research is a few small studies, including a 2024 study of 30 patients who had a peel and a neurotoxin treatment on the same day. Exact ingredient ratios are proprietary.

paras: It is applied by a clinician as an in-office treatment, and the skin peels over the following days. People often pair it with a neurotoxin visit, as in the 30-patient study, and with sunscreen and gentle skincare afterward. Marketing says it suits all skin tones.

Peel side effects include redness, peeling and pigment change. Because it is a medium-depth peel containing phenol and tretinoin, healing takes longer than with a light peel, and product-specific safety data are sparse. People who are pregnant or prone to pigment changes should raise this with the clinician.

angle.text: People use the VI Peel to clear acne marks, fade pigment and sun damage, and smooth fine lines. The multi-acid blend peels away damaged outer skin and the skin renews, leaving a clearer, more even surface. It is marketed for all skin tones, and published data are a few small studies.

lead: The VI Peel is a branded medium-depth chemical peel made by the Vitality Institute. According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated reference, it blends trichloroacetic acid, phenol, salicylic acid, tretinoin and vitamin C, and is marketed for acne, pigmentation, sun damage, acne scarring, melasma and fine lines for all Fitzpatrick skin types.[1]

The same source says the company was founded by emergency physician Abdala Khalil, who developed an initial formulation for his daughter's cystic acne, with a commercial launch around 2005 to 2006 and a body formulation in 2022.[1] These history details come from a single unverified source.
Published research is limited: a 2024 study of 30 patients examined same-day VI Peel and neurotoxin treatment.[2] Exact ingredient ratios are described as proprietary.[1]
infobox: TCA, phenol, salicylic acid, tretinoin, vitamin C

paras: Per Grokipedia, the formula contains TCA, phenol and salicylic acid at about 10 to 12 percent each, tretinoin at 0.1 to 0.4 percent and vitamin C at 4 percent, plus a mineral blend; variants such as Precision Plus and Purify target pigment and acne.[1] The manufacturer is said to describe it as needing no anesthesia and as suitable for darker skin.[1] These are manufacturer-derived claims; independent verification was not found.

Chemical peels as a category are associated with redness, peeling, pigment change and scarring. Product-specific adverse-event data beyond a small 2024 study are not available in the sources reviewed.[2]

A 2024 Journal of Drugs in Dermatology study enrolled 30 patients across Fitzpatrick types I to VI to test whether combining a corrective peel with a neurotoxin on the same day caused extra side effects while improving outcomes.[2] It corresponds to a registered Phase 4 trial (NCT05162300, 2021).[3] A 2014 registered study evaluated microneedling plus the Universal Peel for acne scarring in 15 participants.[4] Sample sizes are small.

timeline.event: Reported launch of the VI Peel.[1]
